minutes.headline: Board heard a clean FY2017 audit, voted to plow the Mass Ave sidewalk, and approved the June 9 Arts Festival.
minutes.summary: The Select Board made appointments, approved an arts festival with public safety and Board of Health conditions, and heard the auditors' report with an unmodified opinion and management letter recommendations. It voted to keep plowing the Massachusetts Avenue sidewalk while pursuing talks with the state highway agency and town counsel. It then heard a quarterly financial report, signed warrants, and received the town manager and committee reports.

what_happened.line: Auditors reported an unmodified opinion on the FY2017 financial statements, with management letter recommendations, including a review of ambulance receivables.
The Board approved the Lunenburg Arts Festival for June 9 on Memorial Drive, with public safety and Board of Health approval as conditions.
A motion to keep plowing the Massachusetts Avenue sidewalk while talks continue with Town Counsel and the state highway agency was recorded; the vote was not audible.
The Board appointed a Historical Commission candidate through June 30, 2021, and reported a town manager raise from executive session.
The land use director and building commissioner will draft a special events license for town counsel review before it returns to the Board.

why_it_matters: The audit points to growing ambulance and tax lien receivables, and to rising pension and OPEB liabilities, all of which bear on future tax bills and on how much free cash is available.
A special events license, if adopted, would set the rules and approvals for future community events such as festivals.
